IMP-001 [P2] [LOGIC_ERROR] [proven] [ticket] -- a replayed soak run drops every config-driven gate, so the churn rule the live run enforces is unreachable in replay
  expected: re-judging a recorded timeline answers the same question the live run answered, so a run that performed no churn cannot read PASS when re-judged
  actual: the replay path builds its config as {replayedFrom, samples} and nothing else. buildVerdict reads churnRequested from config.churnMinutes, so it is false in every replay and the FAIL_NO_CHURN branch is dead code there; soakHours is dropped the same way. One timeline judged twice therefore returns two different verdicts, and the re-judged one is the permissive one
  evidence: scripts/zaicode-soak.mjs builds the replay config at line 266 as {replayedFrom: REPLAY, samples: timeline.length}; scripts/zaicode-soak-verdict.mjs:101 computes churnRequested from config.churnMinutes; demonstrated by evaluating one 23-sample timeline that performed zero churn twice -- with {replayedFrom, samples} it returns PASS with churnTotal 0, with {churnMinutes: 90, soakHours: 12, churnActions: {}, churnErrors: 0} it returns FAIL_NO_CHURN with churnTotal 0

IMP-002 [P3] [LOGIC_ERROR] [proven] [ticket] -- churn rides on the sample, but the sample list is filtered to rows that carry fps, so churn performed on a round whose probe failed is silently dropped
  expected: an interaction the harness actually performed is counted wherever its record landed, so a probe failure cannot erase evidence that the app was exercised
  actual: buildVerdict filters to typeof row.fps === 'number' before tallyChurn and before the churnErrors count, while the harness writes churnActions and churnError onto whichever sample that round produced. A round that churned and then failed its probe therefore contributes nothing to either number, and the tally reads lower than the run performed
  evidence: scripts/zaicode-soak-verdict.mjs:53 filters samples, :97-99 tallies from that filtered list; measured on a 24-row timeline where one row carries probeError and no fps: 48 interactions summed across all rows, 47 across the filtered list -- exactly the one round that both churned and failed its probe

IMP-003 [P2] [LOGIC_ERROR] [proven] [ticket] -- the engine cannot re-create or complete a cycle whose roster it wrote itself: the report file is named after the audit scope, every mutator resolves it by project identity
  expected: a cycle this engine opens is one this engine can finish
  actual: registration names the report saipen_improve_<scope>.md (here SAIPEN, the audit scope), while resolve_report_path and create_report both compute saipen_improve_<project_identity>.md (here vacterro-zaicode). 'improve submit <cycle> <seat> vacterro-zaicode <findings.json>' resolves to a path that does not exist and refuses with 'a strict-cycle report must be created through create_report'; the same submission succeeds with the scope name. The roster's own report_path is the scope form, so the file the engine created is the file the engine will not find
  evidence: tools/improve.py:1610 builds saipen_improve_{_name}.md from the audit scope; tools/improve.py:279 builds it from the project name in resolve_report_path; tools/improve.py:3411 requires the roster's report_path to equal saipen_improve_{project_name}.md. Reproduced live this cycle: submit with vacterro-zaicode REFUSES, submit with SAIPEN returns COMMITTED.
